title: Monte Carlo method
summary: Monte Carlo methods use repeated random sampling to obtain numerical results for deterministic problems. Originating from Stanislaw Ulam's work at Los Alamos, the approach defines an input domain, generates random samples from a probability distribution, runs deterministic computations on each sample, and aggregates the results. The technique is widely applied across science and engineering to solve problems with significant uncertainty, though its accuracy depends on the quality of random number generators and the number of samples used.

mechanisms.title: Random Sampling
mechanisms.explanation: The algorithm generates random inputs from a specified probability distribution over the defined domain. These samples represent possible scenarios for the problem being solved.

mechanisms.title: Result Aggregation
mechanisms.explanation: After running deterministic computations on each random sample, the results are aggregated (typically by averaging or counting) to produce the final numerical estimate. The accuracy improves with the number of samples due to the law of large numbers.
